mainTopic: A כהן גדול and women who are not full בתולות, the child's status as a חלל, and when a כהן becomes טמא for his sister
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב הונא's reading of a ברייתא: a כהן גדול who married the woman he himself raped or seduced must divorce her, and 'he is married' only means he does not pay the קנס. רב אשי challenges this from רב and רבי יוחנן's ruling about a בוגרת and a מוכת עץ, since she would end up that way under him anyway, and the challenge stays a קשיא. Next, the ברייתא says a כהן גדול may not marry another man's אנוסה or מפותה. If he did, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the child is a חלל and the חכמים say the child is כשר, and רב rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. One version links his view to רבי אלעזר, but that runs into a difficulty. So רב אשי explains that they argue whether breaking only a positive commandment makes a חלל, and the גמרא shows how each side reads the word ״אֵלֶּה״ in ויקרא 21:14. Finally, a new ברייתא asks when a כהן becomes טמא for his sister: engaged, forced or seduced, a מוכת עץ, or a בוגרת. The גמרא works through how רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, and then רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, read ״וְלַאֲחוֹתוֹ הַבְּתוּלָה״. It begins to question the second reading, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He does not pay the fine of a seduced woman
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of רב הונא's explanation: 'he is married' only means the כהן גדול does not pay the קנס for seducing her.
steps.simpleTranslation: [What does 'if he married her, he is married' mean? He must divorce her, and 'married' just means] that he does not pay the fine for a seduced woman.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of רב הונא's explanation from the previous page. He says that 'he is married' in the ברייתא only means the כהן גדול is exempt from the קנס of a מפותה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man who seduces a girl and does not marry her pays a fixed fine. Here the כהן גדול did marry her, so he is exempt from the fine, even though, according to רב הונא, he must still divorce her. So 'he is married' does not mean he may stay married. It only means the marriage counts enough to free him from the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine set by the Torah
A girl who was seduced (willing, not forced)
Pays

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'he is married' as 'he may keep her.' רב הונא's whole point is that he must divorce her, and 'married' only matters for the fine.

phrases.english: that he does not pay the fine of a seduced woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין מְשַׁלֵּם קְנָס בִּמְפוּתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's explanation of the ברייתא from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the ברייתא, 'נשוי' means only that he is exempt from the קנס of a מפותה. He must still divorce her.

steps.title: רב אשי objects from the case of a grown woman and one injured by wood
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהה repeats רב הונא's explanation before רב אשי. רב אשי responds by citing רב and רבי יוחנן: a כהן גדול should not marry a בוגרת or a מוכת עץ, but if he did, they stay married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה went from בי כתיל and said this teaching in front of רב אשי. רב אשי said to him: But don't רב and רבי יוחנן both say that a כהן גדול should not marry a grown woman or a woman whose hymen was torn by an accident, but if he did marry her, he is married?
steps.whatsHappening: A story opens: רב גביהה brings רב הונא's explanation to רב אשי. רב אשי pushes back by quoting a ruling that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי quotes a case where the same words, 'if he married, he is married', clearly mean the couple may stay together. That suggests the same words in our ברייתא should mean the same thing. The next step spells out why the two cases are alike.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
In front of him
A girl past the stage of נערות, a grown young woman
A girl whose hymen was torn by an accident, not by relations
'But isn't it…?' Opens a challenge

phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Ketil went,
and said the teaching before Rav Ashi.
phrases.notes: 'The teaching' is רב הונא's explanation from step 1.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא רַב וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it Rav and Rabbi Yochanan
who both say:
A grown woman and one whose hymen was torn by wood: he may not marry her,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן גדול, who must marry a בתולה.

phrases.english: but if he married her, he is married.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא רַב וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's reading of 'נשוי' from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that 'נשוי' means he must divorce her and is only exempt from the קנס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a parallel ruling of רב and רבי יוחנן, the identical phrase 'ואם נשא נשוי' means they may stay married.

steps.title: She would end up that way under him anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the reason behind רב and רבי יוחנן's ruling and applies it to our case. The woman would become a non-virgin while married to him anyway, so after the fact the marriage stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the reason is clear: in the end she would become a grown woman while married to him, and in the end she would lose her virginity while married to him. Here too, in the end she would become a non-virgin while married to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי spells out the logic of his challenge. He draws out the reason for the בוגרת ruling and shows that the same reason fits the כהן גדול's own אנוסה or מפותה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוגרת or a מוכת עץ is only slightly 'less than a virgin.' Any wife will soon grow older and lose her virginity to her husband, so after the fact the marriage stands. The woman this כהן גדול raped or seduced lost her virginity to him, which would have happened in their marriage anyway. So she too should be allowed to stay with him, against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Apparently' or 'so we see'. Draws a conclusion from a source
In the end she will
Literally 'under him': while married to him
'Here too'. Applies the same logic to the current case
A woman who has had relations, a non-virgin

phrases.english: Apparently: she will eventually be a grown woman under him,
she will eventually be one whose hymen is torn under him.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: סוֹפָהּ לִהְיוֹת בְּעוּלָה תַּחְתָּיו.
phrases.english: Here too: she will eventually be a non-virgin under him.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the כהן גדול who married the woman he himself raped or seduced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא: סוֹפָהּ לִהְיוֹת בּוֹגֶרֶת תַּחְתָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind רב אשי's challenge in step 2 and applies it to our ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that the כהן גדול must divorce his own אנוסה or מפותה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is 'she would end up this way under him anyway', the same reason applies to his own אנוסה or מפותה. So 'נשוי' should mean he may keep her.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רב אשי's objection against רב הונא has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the exchange by saying 'קשיא'. רב אשי's challenge to רב הונא is left unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' does not always mean a view is fully rejected, but no answer is given for רב הונא here. The simple reading left standing is that 'נשוי' means the כהן גדול may stay married to his own אנוסה or מפותה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is difficult.' The challenge is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא said the כהן גדול must divorce his own אנוסה or מפותה. רב אשי compared her to a בוגרת or מוכת עץ, who would 'end up this way under him anyway', and the גמרא left this as a קשיא against רב הונא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge raised in steps 2 and 3 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's objection to רב הונא stands unresolved.

steps.title: Another man's raped or seduced woman: is the child a חלל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the ברייתא. A כהן גדול may not marry a woman whom another man raped or seduced. If he did, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the child is a חלל, and the חכמים say the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman raped by another man, or seduced by another man: the כהן גדול may not marry her. If he did marry her, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the child is a חלל, and the חכמים say the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes the next part of the same ברייתא, which records an argument about the child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This woman is different from the last case: she lost her virginity to someone else, not to the כהן גדול. Both sides agree he should not marry her. They argue about whether the child is a חלל, which would mean she counts as a woman forbidden to a כהן גדול in a way that taints the child.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forced by another man
A woman seduced by another man
A child born from a forbidden priestly union, who loses priestly status
Valid, with no flaw in lineage

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same case as steps 1 to 4. There the כהן גדול himself was the one who raped or seduced her. Here it was someone else (חֲבֵירוֹ).

phrases.aramaic: אֲנוּסַת חֲבֵירוֹ וּמְפוּתַּת חֲבֵירוֹ — לֹא יִשָּׂא.
phrases.english: A woman raped by another and a woman seduced by another: he may not marry her.
And if he married her,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: הַוָּלָד חָלָל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: the child is a chalal,
and the Rabbis say: the child is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנוּסַת חֲבֵירוֹ וּמְפוּתַּת חֲבֵירוֹ — לֹא יִשָּׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול may not marry another man's אנוסה or מפותה. Whether the child is a חלל is argued between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the חכמים.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so the child is a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: the הלכה is like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא decides the argument from the previous step. רב, as reported by רב הונא, rules like the single opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the הלכה follows the majority, the חכמים. Here רב rules like the single תנא. So in practice the child of a כהן גדול and another man's אנוסה or מפותה is a חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of…
רב הונא reports a ruling in the name of his teacher רב

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling goes against the usual rule of following the majority. It sets the practical law that the child is a חלל.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument recorded in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the child is a חלל.

steps.title: A second report of the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל also reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, רב גידל said in the name of רב: the הלכה is like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: A second student of רב reports the very same ruling. This confirms that רב really ruled like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two separate reports in רב's name, the ruling is firmly established. The word 'וכן' ('and so too') tells us this is the same ruling heard from another student, not a new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And so too'. Introduces a matching report
An אמורא and student of רב

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול may not marry a woman another man raped or seduced. If he did, רב rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that the child is a חלל, as reported by both רב הונא and רב גידל.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And so too Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 6 with a second report of רב's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two students confirm that רב ruled like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the child is a חלל.

steps.title: A second version: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees with רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: In a different version of רב's teaching, רב explains that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reason is that he agrees with רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it differently: רב הונא said in the name of רב, the reason of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is that he agrees with רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what רב said. Here רב does not give a ruling. He gives the reason behind רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that an unmarried man who lives with an unmarried woman, not for marriage, makes her a זונה. If so, a woman who was raped or seduced counts as a זונה, and a זונה is forbidden to every כהן. That would explain why her child from a כהן גדול is a חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a different version of a teaching
What is the reason?
He holds like (another sage's opinion)

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav Huna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?
He holds like Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר holds that an unmarried man who lives with an unmarried woman, not for marriage, makes her a זונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the ruling version of רב's statement (steps 6-7) with a version that explains the reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view is based on רבי אלעזר's opinion that a woman in an unmarried relationship becomes a זונה.

steps.title: But the הלכה always follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and not רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees with רבי אלעזר. The הלכה always follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, but רב ruled that the הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really agree with him? We hold that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teaching is small in amount but clean, meaning the הלכה always follows him. Yet here רב עמרם said in the name of רב that the הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from the last step by showing that it leads to a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agreed with רבי אלעזר, the הלכה would have to follow רבי אלעזר, because we always rule like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. But רב himself ruled that the הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר. Both statements cannot be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he really hold like him?
We hold as an established rule
A small amount, but clean: few teachings, all of them accepted as הלכה

phrases.english: But does he really hold like him?
But don't we hold as a rule:

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁנַת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב קַב וְנָקִי.
phrases.english: The teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov is a kav, and clean.
phrases.notes: A קב is a small measure. He taught only a little, but the הלכה always follows what he taught.

phrases.english: Whereas about this
Rav Amram said that Rav said:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ? וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees with רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה always follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so if he agreed with רבי אלעזר, the הלכה would follow רבי אלעזר. That contradicts רב's ruling that it does not.

steps.title: The difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the contradiction has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge has no answer, which leaves room for a new explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the problem is real and stays unsolved. The version where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees with רבי אלעזר is left weak, so רב אשי will offer a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: the challenge has no answer

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 9 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explanation that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees with רבי אלעזר remains a difficulty.

steps.title: רב אשי: the argument is whether a positive commandment makes a חלל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the argument differently. The question is whether a child born from a union that breaks only a positive commandment (עשה) is a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: they argue about whether a union that breaks only a positive commandment makes a חלל. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that it does. The חכמים hold that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a brand-new reason for the argument, so there is no need to connect it to רבי אלעזר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A raped or seduced woman is not a זונה. The only problem is that a כהן גדול is commanded to marry a בתולה, and that is a positive commandment (עשה). So the argument turns on one question: does breaking an עשה make the child a חלל?

keyTerms.meaning: Unions forbidden only by a positive commandment (עשה)
They argue about
A child of a כהן who loses the status of כהונה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the woman here counts as a זונה. In רב אשי's approach she is forbidden only because the כהן גדול must marry a בתולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי avoids the unanswered difficulty from step 10, because his reason does not depend on רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
They argue about whether there is a chalal from those who break a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: Here the positive commandment is that a כהן גדול must marry a בתולה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov holds:
There is a chalal from those who break a positive commandment,
and the Rabbis hold:
There is no chalal from those who break a positive commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּיֵשׁ חָלָל מֵחַיָּיבֵי עֲשֵׂה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new explanation of the argument after step 10 left the old one unanswered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: breaking an עשה produces a חלל. The חכמים: it does not.

steps.title: The source: "he shall not profane his seed" refers to all of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns his view. The פסוק about not profaning his seed comes right after the full list, including the command to marry a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reason? The פסוק says: "A widow, a divorcee, a חללה, a זונה, these he shall not take, but only a בתולה..." Then it says: "And he shall not profane his seed among his people." This refers to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's source and answers with two פסוקים in a row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command to marry only a בתולה is a positive commandment. The next פסוק warns that he must not profane his seed. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads that warning as going back on the whole list, including the בתולה command. So marrying a non-virgin also makes the child a חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
And he shall not profane his seed
On all of them

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that a child of a כהן גדול and a non-virgin is a חלל. This is because "ולא יחלל זרעו" applies even to the positive commandment to marry a בתולה. The חכמים disagree.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?
As it is written:
"A widow, or a divorcee, or a chalala, or a zona,
these he shall not take;
but only a virgin, etc."
And it is written:
"And he shall not profane his seed among his people,"
on all of them.
phrases.notes: The warning covers the whole list, even the command to marry only a בתולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב — דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's position as רב אשי explained it in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view that breaking an עשה produces a חלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 21:14-15: "ולא יחלל זרעו" right after "כי אם בתולה", read as applying to all of them.

steps.title: The רבנן: the word ״these″ ends the list
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read ״אֵלֶּה״ as a stopping point, so only the women listed before it make a child a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They say the word ״these″ ends the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 12 showed where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns his view. Now the גמרא shows how the רבנן read the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the list of forbidden women ends with ״אֵלֶּה לֹא יִקָּח״, and only after that comes the command to marry a בתולה. The רבנן say ״אֵלֶּה״ closes the list. So ״וְלֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ״ goes only with the women before it, not with the בתולה command.

keyTerms.meaning: These. The word in the פסוק right after the list of forbidden women.
Ended the topic. It cuts off what comes before from what comes after.
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how the רבנן deal with the proof from Step 12.

phrases.english: "These" ended the topic.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14. ״אֵלֶּה לֹא יִקָּח״ comes before ״כִּי אִם בְּתוּלָה״.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: ״אֵלֶּה״ הִפְסִיק הָעִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוק that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב used in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view that breaking only the עשה of marrying a בתולה does not make the child a חלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word ״אֵלֶּה״ in ויקרא 21:14, which separates the list of forbidden women from the בתולה command.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: ״these″ comes to exclude a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says ״אֵלֶּה״ does not end the list. It teaches that a child from a נדה is not a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said: the word ״these″ comes to exclude a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב answers the רבנן. He gives the word ״אֵלֶּה״ a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״אֵלֶּה״ is needed to teach something else, it is not a stopping point. So the בתולה command still connects to ״וְלֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ״. The word only teaches that ״these″ women make a child a חלל, but a נדה, who is forbidden to everyone and not only to כהנים, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude. To leave a case out of the rule.
A woman in her period of niddah, forbidden to all men until she goes to the מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the word ״אֵלֶּה״ is there. They only argue about what it teaches. The רבנן say it ends the list. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it leaves out a נדה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov said:
"These" comes to exclude a niddah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: ״אֵלֶּה״ לְמַעוֹטֵי נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's reading in Step 13 by giving ״אֵלֶּה״ a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אֵלֶּה״ ends the list, so the בתולה command is not connected to ״וְלֹא יְחַלֵּל״.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אֵלֶּה״ is used to leave out a נדה, so it does not cut off the בתולה command.

steps.title: Whose view does this ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says ״אֵלֶּה″ makes a child a חלל but a נדה does not, and asks whose view it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow? It says: from ״these″ you make a child a חלל, but you do not make a חלל from a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and asks which side it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses ״אֵלֶּה״ to leave out a נדה. That is exactly the reading from Step 14, so the question is pointing toward one side.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
A child of a forbidden כהן marriage who loses כהונה status
That was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Whose view does this teaching follow?
From "these" you make a chalal,
phrases.notes: He means: having a child with the women listed before ״אֵלֶּה״ makes that child a חלל.

phrases.english: but you do not make a chalal from a niddah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a ברייתא that matches the reading in Step 14.

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who uses ״אֵלֶּה״ to leave out a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use ״אֵלֶּה״ to end the list, so they have no extra word to leave out a נדה. Only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads ״אֵלֶּה״ the way the ברייתא does.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

phrases.english: Whose view?
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov's.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Then the תורה should have put ״these″ at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, why not write ״אֵלֶּה״ after the בתולה command?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, let the פסוק write ״these″ at the end!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בתולה command really belongs in the list of things that make a child a חלל, the word ״אֵלֶּה״ should have come after it. Putting ״אֵלֶּה״ before the בתולה command makes it look like the list ends there, which is what the רבנן say.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it write it. The פסוק should have written it this way.
At the end

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
let it write "these" at the end?
phrases.notes: He means after ״כִּי אִם בְּתוּלָה מֵעַמָּיו יִקַּח אִשָּׁה״.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, נִכְתְּבֵיהּ לְ״אֵלֶּה״ לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading from Steps 12 and 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reading that the בתולה command is part of the חלל list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The place of the word ״אֵלֶּה″ in the פסוק points to the list ending before the בתולה command.

steps.title: The question stays difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the question on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the question from Step 17 without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״קַשְׁיָא״ means the challenge is strong and no answer is given. It does not mean רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view is thrown out. It just stays a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question stays with no answer.

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: ״אֵלֶּה״ ends the list, so marrying a non-בתולה does not make a חלל. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: ״אֵלֶּה״ only leaves out a נדה. But the place of ״אֵלֶּה״ in the פסוק stays a difficulty for him.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Step 17 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of why ״אֵלֶּה״ is not written at the end stays unanswered for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Does a כהן become טמא for his engaged sister?
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say a כהן becomes טמא for his engaged sister. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: about his engaged sister, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say he becomes טמא for her. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say he does not become טמא for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא. It is about when a כהן may become טמא to bury his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may become טמא for his sister only if she is a בתולה who was not married (ויקרא 21:3). An engaged woman is still a בתולה but already belongs to a man in some way. That is why there is an argument about her.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught in a ברייתא
His engaged sister, who had קידושין but not yet נישואין
He becomes טמא for her, to take care of her burial

steps.confusionAlert: Here ״אֲרוּסָה״ means engaged, after קידושין. It is not ״אֲנוּסָה״ (a girl who was forced), which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
His betrothed sister,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about a כהן whose sister died, and whether he may become טמא for her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda say:
He becomes impure for her.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
He does not become impure for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֲחוֹתוֹ אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a כהן becoming טמא for his sister.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an argument whether a כהן becomes טמא for his engaged sister.

steps.title: A sister who was forced or seduced
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a כהן does not become טמא for a sister who was forced or seduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was forced or seduced, everyone agrees he does not become טמא for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to a case where there is no argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the engaged sister, this sister is no longer a בתולה. So all four תנאים agree he may not become טמא for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was forced
A woman who was seduced
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: One who was raped or seduced —
all agree he does not become impure for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנוּסָה וּמְפוּתָּה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין מִטַּמֵּא לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case to the ברייתא of Step 19 where everyone agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן does not become טמא for a sister who was forced or seduced.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: she must be fit for a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says a כהן does not become טמא for a sister who lost her virginity by accident, because his rule is that she must be fit for a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a sister who lost her virginity by accident: he does not become טמא for her. These are the words of רבי שמעון. For רבי שמעון used to say: if she is fit for a כהן גדול, he becomes טמא for her. If she is not fit for a כהן גדול, he does not become טמא for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's ruling on a special case, then explains it with his general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוכת עץ never had relations, but she is no longer a full בתולה. רבי שמעון measures the sister by the same test as the woman a כהן גדול may marry. Since a כהן גדול may not marry her, her brother does not become טמא for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who lost her signs of virginity by accident, not through relations
Fit to marry a כהן גדול
For רבי שמעון used to say. It brings his general rule.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the sister's law to the כהן גדול's בתולה rule from the earlier part of the sugya.

phrases.english: And one whose hymen was torn accidentally —
phrases.notes: Literally, "struck by wood." She lost her virginity by an accident, not through relations.

phrases.english: he does not become impure for her,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
For Rabbi Shimon would say:
If she is fit for a High Priest, he becomes impure for her;
if she is not fit for a High Priest —
he does not become impure for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוּכַּת עֵץ — אֵין מִטַּמֵּא לָהּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי שמעון's ruling on מוכת עץ and his general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a כהן becomes טמא for his sister only if she is fit for a כהן גדול.

steps.title: A grown sister: everyone agrees he becomes טמא
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a כהן becomes טמא for his sister who is a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a grown woman: he becomes טמא for her, according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a case where everyone agrees he becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוגרת is a girl who has passed into full adulthood. Even so, all agree she still counts as a בתולה for her brother, and he becomes טמא for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A grown woman, past the age of נערות
According to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: Engaged sister: there is an argument. Forced or seduced: no one allows it. מוכת עץ: רבי שמעון does not allow it. בוגרת: everyone says he becomes טמא for her.

phrases.english: And a grown woman — he becomes impure for her,
according to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבוֹגֶרֶת — מִטַּמֵּא לָהּ, דִּבְרֵי כׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with a case where all agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן becomes טמא for his sister who is a בוגרת, according to everyone.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, who said a כהן becomes טמא for his engaged sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and asks where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה get their ruling from. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה said a כהן becomes טמא for his engaged sister. Now the גמרא wants to see which words in the פסוק lead them there.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A woman who is engaged (betrothed) but not yet fully married

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: This is about their ruling in step 19, that a כהן becomes טמא for his engaged sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 19 to find its source in the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of the פסוק makes רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה include an engaged sister.

steps.title: The word 'virgin' leaves out a sister who was forced or seduced
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה learn from 'ולאחותו הבתולה' that a sister who was forced or seduced is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: They expound it like this: 'And for his virgin sister' leaves out one who was forced or seduced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts giving the reading of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. The word בתולה leaves out a sister who is no longer a virgin because of a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only allows a כהן to become טמא for a sister who is a בתולה. A sister who was אנוסה or מפותה is not a virgin, so she is left out. This matches the rule everyone agreed to in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: They expound (read meaning into the words of the פסוק)
Leaving out; excluding
A woman who was forced
A woman who was seduced

phrases.english: They expound it like this:
"And for his virgin sister"
leaves out one who was forced or seduced.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּדָרְשִׁי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word הבתולה leaves out a sister who was forced or seduced.

steps.title: A sister who lost her virginity by accident is still included
steps.stepSummary: The words 'who has had no man' show that only a sister who lost her virginity through a man is left out, so a מוכת עץ is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should also leave out a sister who lost her virginity by accident. So the פסוק says, 'who has had no man.' Only one who lost it through a man is left out. This one, who did not lose it through a man, is not left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The reading continues. The גמרא shows that a sister who lost her virginity by accident (מוכת עץ) still counts, so her brother does become טמא for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just from the word בתולה, we might think a מוכת עץ is also left out, since she is not physically a virgin. But the words 'אשר לא היתה לאיש' tell us the only thing that matters is whether a man was involved. Since no man was involved for her, she is included, unlike רבי שמעון's view in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
A woman who lost her virginity by accident, not through a man
So the פסוק says (to teach us otherwise)
Her becoming (a non-virgin)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבי שמעון in step 21. Here, by רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, a מוכת עץ IS included and her brother becomes טמא for her.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף מוּכַּת עֵץ —
phrases.english: You might think that I should leave out even one who lost her virginity by accident.
So the verse says: "who has had no man."
The one left out is one who stopped being a virgin through a man.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאָה זוֹ שֶׁאֵין הֲוָיָיתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אִישׁ.
phrases.english: This one is not left out, because she did not stop being a virgin through a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף מוּכַּת עֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the exclusion from step 24 so that it does not cover a מוכת עץ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אשר לא היתה לאיש' shows that only a loss of virginity through a man disqualifies, so a מוכת עץ is included.

steps.title: 'Who is near' includes an engaged sister, and 'to him' includes a בוגרת
steps.stepSummary: The word 'הקרובה' adds an engaged sister, and 'אליו' adds a sister who is a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who is near' comes to include an engaged sister. 'To him' comes to include a grown woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reading of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. Here is their actual source that a כהן becomes טמא for his engaged sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הקרובה adds a ארוסה, which is the main ruling of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה from step 19. The word אליו adds a בוגרת, which matches what everyone agreed in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is near (to him)
To include; to add
A girl past the age of נערה, a grown young woman

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, a כהן becomes טמא for his sister if she is a מוכת עץ, a ארוסה, or a בוגרת. Only אנוסה and מפותה are left out.

phrases.english: "Who is near" comes to include the engaged sister.
"To him" comes to include the grown woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקְּרוֹבָה לְרַבּוֹת הָאֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקרובה includes a ארוסה, and אליו includes a בוגרת.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר need a פסוק to include a בוגרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed for a בוגרת, since רבי מאיר holds that the word בתולה already means even a partial virgin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse for this? Didn't רבי מאיר say that 'virgin' means even someone who is partly a virgin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last part of the reading. It says the word אליו seems to be extra for רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds elsewhere that the word בתולה covers even 'מקצת בתולה', someone who is only partly a virgin, like a בוגרת. If so, the word בתולה in our פסוק already includes a בוגרת. Then why does he need the extra word אליו?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a פסוק?
Partly a virgin
It implies; it means

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse for this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means including the בוגרת through the word אליו.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Meir say:
"Virgin" means even someone who is partly a virgin!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְמָה לִי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for 'אליו' from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of אליו to include a בוגרת by רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר holds that בתולה already includes a partial virgin, so the extra word looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The פסוק is needed to block a גזירה שוה from the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The extra word is needed, because otherwise we might learn from the כהן גדול that 'בתולה' here means only a נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: let us learn 'virgin' here from 'virgin' there. Just as there it means a young girl, so too here it means a young girl. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra word אליו is really needed. Without it, we would have made a comparison that leaves out the בוגרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בתולה also appears about the woman a כהן גדול must marry, and there it means only a נערה. Without אליו, we might have used a גזירה שוה to say that בתולה here also means only a נערה. The word אליו stops that and makes sure a בוגרת is included.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
You might have thought
Let us learn (one case from another)
A young girl, before becoming a בוגרת
So it teaches us (otherwise)

phrases.english: It was needed,
because you might have thought
let us learn "virgin" here from "virgin" there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is the פסוק about the כהן גדול, who must marry a בתולה.

phrases.english: just as there it means a young girl,
so too here it means a young girl.
So the verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra word is needed to block a mistaken גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would compare בתולה here to בתולה by the כהן גדול, and limit it to a נערה.
steps.terutzMaskana: אליו teaches that a כהן becomes טמא even for a sister who is a בוגרת.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, who say a כהן does not become טמא for his engaged sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the ברייתא. This line sets up their reading of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון said a כהן does not become טמא for his engaged sister. The גמרא now wants to see how they read the same words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ —
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon, what is their reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first side of the ברייתא to the second side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון read the פסוק so that an engaged sister is left out.

steps.title: 'Who has had no man' leaves out an engaged sister
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון leave out a sister who was forced, seduced, or a מוכת עץ, and they also leave out an engaged sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: They expound it like this: 'And for his virgin sister' leaves out one who was forced, seduced, or lost her virginity by accident. 'Who has had no man' leaves out an engaged sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reading of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון. They use the same words, but they read them differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For them, the word בתולה leaves out even a מוכת עץ, which fits רבי שמעון in step 21. They read 'אשר לא היתה לאיש' as leaving out a sister who already 'belongs to a man' through engagement. This is the source for their ruling that a כהן does not become טמא for his ארוסה sister.

keyTerms.meaning: Who has not been (to a man)

steps.confusionAlert: The same words 'אשר לא היתה לאיש' are read in two ways. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה use them to include a מוכת עץ. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון use them to leave out a ארוסה.

phrases.english: They expound it like this:
"And for his virgin sister"
leaves out one who was forced, seduced, or lost her virginity by accident.
"Who has had no man" leaves out an engaged sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרְשִׁי הָכִי וְלַאֲחוֹתוֹ הַבְּתוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 with a different reading of the same פסוק used in steps 24 to 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בתולה leaves out אנוסה, מפותה, and מוכת עץ. 'אשר לא היתה' leaves out a ארוסה.

steps.title: 'Who is near' includes a divorced ארוסה, and 'to him' includes a בוגרת
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, הקרובה adds an engaged sister who was divorced, and אליו adds a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who is near' comes to include an engaged sister who was divorced. 'To him' comes to include the grown woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reading of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון. A sister who was engaged and then divorced is 'near' to her brother again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'אשר לא היתה' already left out a ארוסה, these sages use הקרובה for a different case: a ארוסה who was divorced. Like the other side, they use אליו to include a בוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Who was divorced

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, a כהן does not become טמא for his sister if she is אנוסה, מפותה, מוכת עץ, or ארוסה. He does become טמא for a divorced ארוסה and for a בוגרת.

phrases.english: "Who is near" comes to include an engaged sister who was divorced.
"To him" comes to include the grown woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקְּרוֹבָה לְרַבּוֹת אֲרוּסָה שֶׁנִּתְגָּרְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון that began in step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקרובה includes a divorced ארוסה, and אליו includes a בוגרת.

steps.title: The גמרא repeats 'who is near' to question it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again that הקרובה includes a divorced ארוסה, so that it can challenge this reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who is near' comes to include an engaged sister who was divorced?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the last reading, this time as a question. This line sets up a challenge that continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new teaching. The גמרא quotes the reading of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון again because it is about to ask how הקרובה can really include a divorced ארוסה.

phrases.english: "Who is near"
comes to include an engaged sister who was divorced?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקְּרוֹבָה לְרַבּוֹת אֲרוּסָה שֶׁנִּתְגָּרְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes step 31 again in order to challenge it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that הקרובה includes a divorced ארוסה, by רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Questions whether the word הקרובה can really be the source for a divorced ארוסה. The full challenge continues past this part.
